text: The doctor was nice, and some of the receptionists were okay. But this is from my own experience: I got braces at this clinic, and my brackets came off very often. I think the doctor wasn't the owner of the clinic, but I'm not sure. In the first month, on the first day, I came home and ate Pad Thai, and a bracket came off! I barely ate any hard food, but two brackets came off in the first month. What was most frustrating was that it happened while eating Pad Thai! It happened on the very first day. It happened every month, and the brackets that came off were those that had changed position. For example, if the bracket on a tooth changed position, the next month it would be gone. That was it! A relative of mine got braces from a different male doctor, and they ate even more hard food, but none of their brackets came off.

text:
I've used their services three times.
The first time, the service was good and on time.
The second time, my appointment was at 1:00 PM. I arrived at the clinic at 12:50 PM but had to wait almost 30 minutes. The reason given was that the patient before me was already being treated and the dentist was on a lunch break (I understood that).
The third time, my appointment was at 3:30 PM. I arrived at the clinic at 3:20 PM. The front desk staff said, "Please wait. There's still a patient in the room getting dentures done, and there's another patient waiting for a filling." They also said I should wait approximately 30-45 minutes.

**I'd like to suggest to the clinic that they be aware of the patient's oral health issues and how long each appointment takes. If there are walk-in cases, they should be informed. Appointments should be kept on time. Normally, there might be slight delays of 5-10 minutes, which I understand. But this time, I felt like the clinic accepted all the patients and then made the customers feel frustrated by the long wait.**

***A scheduling system should improve efficiency. Please improve this aspect of your appointment.
